descripcion_geo: Southern region of Mesopotamia, at the mouth of the Tigris and Euphrates. Headquarters of the Neo-Babylonian Empire.
importancia_estrategica: Capital of world power in the 7th-6th centuries BC; conquered Jerusalem and deported Judah.

historias.descripcion: The Chaldean king Nebuchadnezzar sacks the Temple, demolishes the walls of Jerusalem and deports the people to Babylon.
Daniel and his companions are taken to Babylon; Daniel interprets the king's dreams and survives the fiery furnace.
Cyrus the Great conquers Babylon without battle; Jews in exile are freed to return to their land.

personajes.descripcion: He conquered Jerusalem, destroyed the Temple, and deported the people of Judah.
Jewish scholar at the Chaldean court; His visions span empires to the end time.
During their banquet the hand that wrote on the wall appeared; Babylon fell that night.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: Cradle of astrology and magic; The Babylonian exile transformed Judaism: the synagogue, the codification of the Torah and exclusive monotheism emerged.

judaismo.descripcion: Mene, Tekel, Paris: Daniel interprets the signs that announce the end of the Chaldean kingdom.

islam.descripcion: Babylon appears in the Quran as a place of punishment for those who practiced magic (Cor 2:102).
